subject: Post-demo recap: Acme observability & operational tooling comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: Acme observability & operational tooling comparison

Hi John thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our discussion: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goals: reduce inference unit cost by ~30% for peak traffic, get per-route latency SLOs, and get tracing/observability across model variants.
- Constraints: must integrate with existing Datadog/Tracing stack, strict retention for audit logs, and procurement timeline targets Nov 30.

2) How Redwood maps to your needs (short version)
- Observability: per-model & per-route dashboards, token-level latency+cost breakdowns, and automatic regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
- Tracing: open tracing hooks + Datadog export; we support request-level trace IDs and span annotations (you can correlate model token spans to service traces).
- Cost controls: intelligent batching + KV/prefix caching and quantization recommendations to lower per-token costs without sacrificing quality.
- Reliability: smart routing (region/fallback/variant) and canary rollouts for model updates.

3) Competitive notes you asked for vs hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) and other inference APIs
- Hyperscalers (e.g., SageMaker/Vertex): strong infra elasticity but limited built-in model-aware observability (no token-level breakdowns) and vendor lock-in around their endpoint semantics.
- Other inference APIs: simpler integration but fewer runtime controls (batching, cache, routing) and less transparent unit economics.
- Practical impact: for your bursty RLHF workloads, Redwood's prefix/KV caching + continuous batching typically reduces p99 cost by 20–40% vs a naive endpoint on hyperscaler infra.

4) Proposed tests/next steps
- Short perf test: we’ll provide an eval harness to run 1k synthetic requests across your common prompt shapes (latency, throughput, cost).
- Observability check: we’ll ship a sample trace+datadog integration and a prebuilt dashboard you can drop into your account.
- Security: send over your security contact and we’ll surface SOC2 artifacts + data retention options.

Attachments: redwood-acme-observability-comparison.pdf (short side-by-side), mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx (timeline).

Are you available Mon/Tue morning PST for the perf run? I’ll loop in our SE (Priyom) to own the test.

Best,
Marissa

Also, looping in our security team (security@acme-corp.com) they’ll want SOC2 + encryption-in-transit docs.

Thanks John short answers and who's owning what:

- Tracing/Datadog: yes, we support span-level token timing. Priyom (cc’d) will send the Datadog agent config and a sample trace export that annotates token spans.
- Retention/export: both Dedicated and Private deployments support configurable retention and S3 export of logs; for Hosted we can provide audit exports but Dedicated/Private are recommended for 1yr retention and strict export policies. Rishi will connect on procurement/packaging options for Dedicated (cost & timeline).
- Eval keys: we can issue timeboxed eval API keys (TTL default 7 days, configurable). Quotas can be set per key and we’ll provision the keys scoped to the perf harness.

Priyom can you take point on the perf harness (latency/throughput scripts, sample dashboard, datadog config)? Rishi can you prepare a Dedicated skus/options doc for Acme (monthly commit + expected p99 SLO tiers)?

Next meeting: Mon 11/09 9:30am PST to kick off perf run (tentative). If that doesn’t work we’ll shift to Tue 11/10.
